source_admission: Values come from a bounded lookup of 15 November 2026 (about 16 minutes, 34 sources: 10 read, 6 through an automated reader, 18 from an abstract or summary). Its record, with every value's locator and label, is kept on the research drive in session-tools/agents/south_sea_salt (values.md, sources.json). No outside dataset or full paper is committed. Each value below carries one of these labels: read (in the source's own table or text, extracted from the paper's file), read_via (in a later paper that tabulates the primary value), summary (abstract or search summary only), computed (one division of read values), recalled (not looked up) or project (a product or document of this repository). Earth values are reference points, never bounds on the lunar case.

seawater_g_per_kg.evidence: recalled by the lookup; equal, to the figures given, to the composition the sea chemistry study carries

seawater_density_kg_m3.evidence: project: UNESCO EOS-80 at 29.5 C and practical salinity 35, as the seawater lakes study on domain/hydrosphere computes it

cl_ppm.evidence: read: Table 6, 717 +/- 110 ppm; the 600-800 span covers Orgueil by instrumental activation, 600 +/- 74 (PalmeZipfel2022, read_via), and Ryugu, 776 +/- 21 (read_via)

cl_ppm_disputed_low.evidence: read_via LoddersFegley2023 Tables 5-6: Orgueil 115 +/- 36 ppm from two samples of 1-2 mg by neutron irradiation and noble-gas mass spectrometry; the compilers reject it on stated analytical grounds; the 2017 paper itself was not opened

n_ppm.evidence: read: 2500 +/- 660 (2021, Table 1); computed about 2000 from the 2025 atomic ratio with silicon at 10.77 wt%

h_ppm.evidence: read: Table 1, 18600 +/- 3440; counted wholly as water it is 16.6 wt%

water_soluble_share_of_cl.note: about a third in one Orgueil analysis (Sharp et al. 2013, read_via); fresh falls suggest more; a working reading, no published group value

other_chondrites_cl_ppm.evidence: read: Table 1; uncertainties for the halogens are stated as considerably larger than ten percent

cl_per_water_by_mass.evidence: computed from HCl/H2O = 1.4e-4 by number (Rubin2019 Table 2, read); the range was decoded from a garbled extraction and needs checking against the paper's file; gas phase only, so a lower bound on the nucleus

cl_per_n_gas.evidence: computed from Cl/O = 1.19e-4 and N/O = 8.51e-3 by number in the volatiles (Table 3, read)

cl_per_n_gas_over_gas_and_dust_nitrogen.evidence: computed from Table 4 for dust-to-ice ratios of 3 and 1; the dust's chlorine is unmeasured, so a floor

cl_per_water_solar_ceiling.evidence: computed: the gas value scaled to the protosolar Cl/O

comet_ice.note: No published bulk chlorine for a comet nucleus counts gas, ammonium salts and dust together. Ammonium chloride led the salts seen in one dust grain of comet 67P (Altwegg2020, read), and at least one further chlorine carrier is unidentified (Dhooghe2021, read).

na_weight_fraction_highland_soil.evidence: computed from Na2O 0.46-0.50 wt% (Table 7.15, read): Apollo 16 and Luna 20 soil averages

cl_ppm_rock.evidence: read: Table 1; mare basalts 1.9-10.0 ppm water-soluble plus 1.1-5.8 ppm bound, three anorthosites averaging 9 ppm; 65 +/- 10% water-soluble in the basalts

cl_ppm_soil.evidence: computed from a general statement (vapour-mobilised elements in soils are 10-100 times below CI), no chlorine measurement of soils was reached

kuiper_belt_small_bodies_kg.evidence: project: resources/README.md, finding 1, from Pitjeva & Pitjev 2018
